# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

tests/test_merge.py

   4|     Input may be unsorted. Returns a sorted list of tuples."""

content: All tests pass and edge cases behave correctly: touching intervals merge, unsorted input is handled, nested intervals collapse, and empty input returns `[]`.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py`: the merge condition `start < last_end` was changed to `start <= last_end` so closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. (1,3) and (3,5)) merge into (1,5), and the input is now fully sorted before merging so unsorted input is handled correctly. Rewrote the loop to iterate over `sorted(intervals)` and build the merged list from scratch, avoiding the previous bug where `intervals[0]` was used unsorted and would have been processed twice. Verified with the existing test suite (2 tests pass) plus manual checks for unsorted, nested, point, and empty inputs.
